stories.title: Automated Factory Builder Hadrian Raises $1.37B in Series D Round
stories.excerpt: Hadrian ,a Torrance-based advanced manufacturing company building highly automated factories, has raised $1.37 billion in Series D financing. The capital raise values Hadrian at $7.87 billion. The company said it will use the financing to construct new factories, expand its research and development and advance its artificial intelligence-powered production capabilities. WCM Investment Management, Washington Harbour Partners, Valor Equity Partners, 137 Ventures and Baillie Gifford are co-leading the financing round, which has been joined by JPMorganChase’s Strategic Investment Group as anchor co-lead. “This financing allows Hadrian to accelerate building the Factories of the Future, expand into new mission-critical production capabilities, and invest in the technicians and engineers who will rebuild America’s industrial base,” said Chris Power, founder and CEO of Hadrian Since its Series C financing 12 months ago, Hadrian has opened new factories in Mesa, AZ and Muscle Shoals, AL, bringing its footprint to just under three million square feet across four sites The post Automated Factory Builder Hadrian Raises $1.37B in Series D Round appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hadrian raises $1.37B Series D at $7.87B valuation for advanced manufacturing factories
Company expanding footprint: Mesa AZ and Muscle Shoals AL opened since Series C; now ~3M SF across four sites
Capital targets factory construction, R&D, and AI-powered production scaling
stories.summary: Hadrian, a Torrance-based factory automation company, closed a $1.37 billion Series D round co-led by WCM Investment Management, Washington Harbour Partners, Valor Equity Partners, and JPMorgan Chase's Strategic Investment Group, valuing the company at $7.87 billion. The company plans to use proceeds to construct new factories, expand R&D, and advance AI capabilities. Since its Series C 12 months prior, Hadrian has opened new facilities in Mesa, Arizona and Muscle Shoals, Alabama, growing its footprint to just under 3 million square feet across four sites.
stories.impact: Massive capital influx into advanced manufacturing reshores signals sustained demand for industrial real estate in emerging manufacturing hubs (Mesa, Muscle Shoals), particularly for large-format, high-clearance facilities. This venture-backed industrial expansion may intensify competition for land and development opportunities in secondary manufacturing markets and compress available pipeline for traditional industrial developers.

stories.title: Newmark Arranges Full-Building Lease for Dynamic Manufacturing in Forest Park
stories.excerpt: Newmark has arranged a long-term, full-building industrial lease totaling 150,316 square feet on behalf of the tenant, Dynamic Manufacturing, at 7801 Industrial Drive in Forest Park, Illinois. Newmark Senior Managing Director Corey Chase represented the tenant in the lease negotiations. The landlord is First Industrial Realty Trust, Inc. Dynamic Manufacturing will utilize the facility for industrial warehousing, electrification and manufacturing operations, providing the company with additional warehouse capacity. Located on 5.07 acres, 7801 Industrial Drive features 4,509 square feet of office space, 24-foot clear heights, six interior loading docks, one drive-in door and parking for 120 vehicles. Situated approximately 10 miles west of downtown Chicago with immediate access to Interstates 290 and 294, the property offers efficient connectivity throughout the Chicago metropolitan area and to regional transportation networks. Its infill location provides access to a deep labor pool and proximity to major manufacturing, distribution and logistics corridors throughout the Midwest. The tenant will use the First Industrial Realty Trust property for industrial warehousing, electrification, and manufacturing operations. The 5.07-acre facility offers 24-foot clear heights, six interior loading docks, one drive-in door, and parking for 120 vehicles, with immediate access to Interstates 290 and 294 and proximity to major Midwest manufacturing and logistics corridors.
stories.impact: Full-building lease absorption in Chicago's westside industrial market (Forest Park/I-290 corridor) signals sustained demand for manufacturing and light-industrial space, particularly for electrification operations. For developers, this validates continued strength in Class B/C industrial assets near labor pools and transportation hubs in legacy manufacturing submarkets like Chicagoland.

stories.title: 960K-SF Speculative Industrial Development in Columbus Breaks Ground
stories.excerpt: Trident Capital Group and O’Connor Capital Partners announced the closing of a joint venture with Clarion Partners for the next phase of its Rickenbacker Industrial Center, a 959,579 square-foot speculative industrial facility located at 1669 Rohr Road in Columbus, Ohio. The partners also announced that construction has broken ground on the project, with delivery targeted for the first quarter of 2027. The building is being marketed for lease by JLL’s Dan Wendorf, Brian Marsh, and Joseph Davis. Situated on 57.30 acres, the project will feature 40-foot clear heights, 104 dock doors, 238 trailer parking stalls, and 336 car parking spaces. The building sits within a designated Qualified Opportunity Zone and carries a 15-year, 75% property tax abatement.The site is located within the broader Rickenbacker industrial corridor, home to corporate distribution and logistics operations for companies including Amazon, ODW Logistics, PepsiCo, Whirlpool, Coca-Cola, AmerisourceBergen, Geodis, and Cardinal Health. stories.summary: Trident Capital Group and O'Connor Capital Partners announced closing of a joint venture with Clarion Partners for the next phase of Rickenbacker Industrial Center in Columbus, Ohio—a 959,579-square-foot speculative industrial facility on 57.30 acres at 1669 Rohr Road. Construction has broken ground with delivery targeted for Q1 2027. The building will feature 40-foot clear heights, 104 dock doors, and 238 parking spaces, marketed for lease by JLL's Dan Wendorf, Brian Marsh, and Joseph Davis.
stories.impact: Speculative industrial development breaking ground in Columbus signals developer confidence in Midwest logistics demand and reflects shift toward larger-format, dock-heavy facilities for third-party logistics and e-commerce fulfillment. This pipeline addition pressures existing industrial assets in Columbus and indicates tight market conditions warranting new supply; developers should monitor pre-leasing velocity to gauge post-delivery absorption risk.

stories.title: Link Logistics Acquires 400K-SF Industrial Asset in Louisville
stories.excerpt: Link Logistics, an operator of last-mile industrial real estate and warehouse properties, announced the addition to its portfolio of a 402,444-square-foot industrial asset located at 5100 Jeff Commerce Drive in Louisville, Kentucky. Link Logistics was represented by CBRE in the transaction. The seller was represented by NAI Fortis and Lee & Associates. Located in Louisville’s Southside/Airport submarket, the property offers proximity to UPS Worldport, GE Appliance Park and the Ford Assembly Plant. “Our investment strategy is focused on expanding Link Logistics’ presence in markets that offer long-term relevance to our customers and their supply chains,” said Andrew Goodman, senior managing director, Investments, Link Logistics. “This addition reflects our continued conviction in Louisville, a market supported by durable demand drivers and strong connectivity to major logistics and manufacturing hubs.” Hear from the West Coast’s Leading Industrial Real Estate Experts | August 20Gain firsthand insight from the executives, investors, and developers navigating today’s industrial market. stories.summary: Link Logistics, an operator of last-mile industrial real estate and warehouse properties, acquired a 402,444-square-foot industrial asset at 5100 Jeff Commerce Drive in Louisville, Kentucky, located in the Southside/Airport submarket. The property offers proximity to UPS Worldport, GE Appliance Park, and the Ford Assembly Plant. Link Logistics was represented by CBRE; the seller was represented by NAI Fortis and Lee & Associates.
stories.impact: Institutional operator's strategic acquisition in Louisville reflects sustained conviction in supply-chain-anchored submarkets. The targeting of assets near UPS Worldport and major OEM facilities (Ford, GE) signals continued strength in last-mile and logistics-oriented industrial demand; this validates Louisville as a long-term multifamily migration driver due to correlated job growth in logistics, warehousing, and light manufacturing.

stories.title: Newmark Arranges $312M Sale of Plaza District Office Tower
stories.excerpt: Newmark said Friday it has advised on the sale and arranged $155 million in acquisition financing for 10 E. 53rd St., a 385,224-square-foot Class A office tower in Manhattan’s Plaza District. Meadow Partners acquired the property from seller SL Green Realty Corp. for $312 million. The acquisition loan was provided by Corebridge Financial, according to published reports. Co-Head of U.S. Capital Markets Adam Spies, Executive Vice Chairman Adam Doneger and Executive Managing Director Avery Silverstein advised the seller, while Co-Head of Global Debt & Structured Finance Jordan Roeschlaub, Vice Chairman Nick Scribani, Director Tim Polglase and Analysts Stavros Giannakopoulos and Lance Tillman secured the financing with Corebridge. The sale ends a hold period that lasted nearly 15 years. SL Green acquired 10 E. 53rd in early 2012 for $252.5 million and invested $67 million in capital improvements during its ownership. The property’s tenant roster includes Equinox, Magnetar, Urban Compass and Ermenegildo Zegna The post Newmark Arranges $312M Sale of Plaza District Office Tower appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: SL Green sells 10 E. 53rd St, 385,224-SF Plaza District office tower, for $312M after 15-year hold
Meadow Partners acquires from SL Green; Corebridge Financial provides $155M acquisition financing
SL Green realized $59.5M gain on $252.5M 2012 purchase plus $67M capex investment
stories.summary: Newmark advised on the sale of 10 E. 53rd Street, a 385,224-square-foot Class A office tower in Manhattan's Plaza District, for $312 million. Meadow Partners acquired the property from SL Green Realty Corp., which had held it for nearly 15 years since acquiring it in early 2012 for $252.5 million and investing $67 million in capital improvements. Corebridge Financial provided a $155 million acquisition loan.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. However, the long-hold liquidation and modest pricing on a repositioned Class A asset reflects continued weakness in Manhattan office fundamentals and capital flight by institutional office investors; this may signal broader CRE capital reallocation away from legacy office toward residential, industrial, and mixed-use projects in primary and secondary markets.

stories.title: Longfellow Sells Hatch Life Sciences Building in LIC for $87M
stories.excerpt: Life sciences developer Longfellow Real Estate Partners has parted with its first-ever New York City project at a discount. Longfellow’s Hatch Life Sciences Building, located at 43-10 23 Street in Long Island City, Queens, has sold for $86.9 million, according to city records filed Friday. Pearl Realty Management’s Jack Guttman signed for the buyer, under the entity 4310 23 St. A representative of Pearl Realty Management did not respond to requests for comment. Longfellow purchased the existing building at 43-10 23 Street in 2021 alongside its partner, Steven Orbuch’s Sculptor Real Estate, for $92.5 million. Longfellow, led by CEO and co-founder Adam Sichol, planned to invest another $120 million into turning the former parachute manufacturing plant into a mix of life sciences labs and offices. Construction had all but wrapped up when Commercial Observer visited in 2024. The final product spanned over 208,000 square feet across seven floors, including prebuilt lab suites, modular research space and flexible office areas. Longfellow and Sculptor did not respond immediately to requests for comment on the sale. While Guttman’s plans for the purchase remain unclear, the landlord appears to be active in the Long Island City market. Recent purchases include the Standard Motors Product Building at 37-18 Northern Boulevard for $42 million and BrightSpire Capital‘s office building at 21-02 49th Avenue for $28 million. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Longfellow Real Estate sells Hatch Life Sciences Building in Long Island City for $86.9M at $3.6M loss
Project purchased 2021 for $92.5M with partner Sculptor Real Estate; $120M planned capex on life sciences conversion
Pearl Realty Management entity acquires 208,000-SF mixed lab and office asset at completion
stories.summary: Life sciences developer Longfellow Real Estate Partners sold its Hatch Life Sciences Building at 43-10 23rd Street in Long Island City, Queens, for $86.9 million—a loss of approximately $5.6 million against its $92.5 million 2021 acquisition price and planned $120 million capital investment. The developer had partnered with Steven Orbuch's Sculptor Real Estate on the acquisition. The 208,000-square-foot property spans seven floors with prebuilt lab suites, modular research space, and flexible office areas. Pearl Realty Management's entity acquired the stabilized asset.
stories.impact: Significant red flag for life sciences real estate in NYC: a developer with expertise in the sector selling at a loss despite project completion signals oversupply, tenant absorption challenges, or cap rate compression in LIC life sciences market. This reflects tightening in specialized biotech/pharma R&D leasing and suggests caution for developers considering life sciences conversions in high-cost outer boroughs; multifamily or flex-use alternatives may face similar headwinds in LIC.

stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Buys Two Miami Affordable Housing Rentals
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has acquired two affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County from the Gatehouse Group, paying a combined $63.8 million, property records show. In the largest deal, the investor paid $34 million for the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments in the Naranja neighborhood, near the southern end of the county. Built in 2011, the 4.8-acre asset houses 20 three-story buildings at 25881 Southwest 143rd Court, just west of the South Dixie Highway. The sale breaks down to roughly $226,660 per unit. CBRE Capital Partners provided a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan. Across the county in Miami’s Little River neighborhood, Starwood paid $29.75 million for the 160-unit Lafayette Square complex. The 19-story building sits on a 1.2-acre site, a block west from Northeast Second Avenue at 150 Northeast 79th Street. The deal equates to about $185,900 per apartment. The Gatehouse Group appears to have retained ownership of the adjacent 136-unit property. The Mansfield, Mass.-based firm developed both the Lafayette Square and Magnolia Landing Apartments, completing the former in 2008 and the latter in 2011. Representatives for Starwood and Gatehouse Group did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management acquires two affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County from Gatehouse Group for $63.8M combined
Magnolia Landing Apartments, Naranja: 150 units, $34M ($226,660/unit); Lafayette Square, Little River: 160 units, $29.75M ($185,900/unit)
CBRE Capital Partners provided $23.8M Freddie Mac loan; both properties built 2010s era with long-term affordability covenants
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management acquired two affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County from the Gatehouse Group for a combined $63.8 million. Magnolia Landing Apartments in Naranja (150 units, 4.8 acres, built 2011) sold for $34 million ($226,660 per unit), while Lafayette Square in Little River (160 units, 19-story building, 1.2 acres) sold for $29.75 million ($185,900 per unit). CBRE Capital Partners provided a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan for the Naranja deal.
stories.impact: Starwood's acquisition of two Miami-Dade affordable properties signals institutional capital rotation into workforce/affordable housing—a segment often benefiting from tax credits, Freddie Mac financing, and stable cash flows. This validates Miami as a multifamily growth market and suggests developers should explore affordable/mixed-income production with subsidy programs (9% LIHTC, Freddie Mac loans) as a supply strategy alongside market-rate development in hot Florida submarkets.

stories.title: Ad Agency Doubles Office HQ Space in Move to Hackman Campus in L.A.
stories.excerpt: An international advertising agency is more than doubling its office footprint with a new headquarters lease in El Segundo, Calif. Innocean USA signed the 101,000-square-foot deal at Hackman Capital Partners’ creative office campus in the small enclave just south of Los Angeles International Airport. The agency will relocate nearly 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach after construction on its new space concludes in 2027, according to JLL, which represented the tenant. The company reportedly will use part of the space as a production facility for commercials and other content. Terms of the lease were not disclosed. “This move is about creating the right environment for our next chapter,” Innocean USA CEO Steve Jun said in a statement. “This is an investment in our people, our clients, and the future we’re building together.” The complex, named after its address at 888 Douglas Street, includes four buildings totaling 550,000 square feet over 30 acres. Hackman acquired the former Northrop Grumman aerospace manufacturing complex in 2016, and invested about $100 million converting it into the creative office. Other major occupiers at the property have included L’Oréal USA, which signed for more than 100,000 square feet in 2021, and Beyond Meat, which originally leased 280,000 square feet for its headquarters. Aerospace and defense companies have also returned to L.A.’s South Bay, and helped bolster leasing at the El Segundo campus. Hypersonic aircraft developer Hermeus signed for 62,552 square feet earlier this year, while Varda Space Industries expanded to 54,749 square feet in 2025. Innocean USA is the U.S. arm of Innocean Worldwide, which was created by Hyundai Motor Group. JLL’s Jason Fine, Jeff Ingham and Mitch Lundquist represented Innocean, while Hackman was represented in-house. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Innocean USA signs 101,000-SF office lease at Hackman Capital's El Segundo creative campus; relocates ~600 employees
Tenant doubling footprint from 50,000 SF in Huntington Beach; delivery 2027; includes commercial production facility
Hackman's 888 Douglas Street: 550,000 SF across four buildings, 30 acres, former Northrop Grumman aerospace site
stories.summary: International advertising agency Innocean USA signed a 101,000-square-foot office lease at Hackman Capital Partners' creative office campus (888 Douglas Street) in El Secondo, California, just south of LAX. The company will relocate approximately 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach, more than doubling its footprint. The new space will include a production facility for commercials and other content, with construction concluding in 2027. Hackman's complex includes four buildings totaling 550,000 square feet over 30 acres.
stories.impact: Corporate relocation and workplace expansion in El Segundo signals tech/media-services job growth in South LA and validates Hackman's repurposed aerospace real estate as a destination for creative tenants. For multifamily developers, this underscores rising employment and talent concentration in South Bay/LAX corridor, creating demand for workforce housing; El Segundo and adjacent beach communities may see stronger renter demand and wage-supported rent growth over next 2–3 years.

stories.title: Attorney James Allen Joins Camber Property Group as Senior Counsel
stories.excerpt: Camber Property Group has onboarded a new general counsel for its affordable housing and community development transactions, Commercial Observer has learned. James Allen has decamped from real estate law firm Hirschen Singer & Epstein and started the new role this week assisting Camber with affordable housing projects in New York state and the New York tri-state region, according to the development firm. “One trend I am seeing is that, in their efforts to solve the ongoing housing affordability crisis, more developers are starting to expand both the types of projects that they participate in and their geographic footprint,” Allen said in a statement. “Camber is always thinking creatively about both, but they present unique challenges.” Allen was previously an associate for four years at Nixon Peabody and a senior staff attorney for the New York Court of Appeals. The Brooklyn Law School graduate also pens articles about housing equity and affordability while serving on the board of the New York Housing Conference’s Rising Leaders Network and the New York City Bar Association’s Housing & Urban Development Committee. Hirschen Singer & Epstein did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “I feel lucky to have the chance to expand upon that and work with many of the legal partners that I have learned from over the years, while Camber solidifies its New York presence and intentionally expands its footprint to other regions,” Allen said. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: James Allen hired as Senior Counsel at Camber Property Group for affordable housing and community development
Allen joins from law firm Hirschen Singer & Epstein; will focus on NY state and tri-state region projects
Indicates developer expansion of affordable housing and geographic footprint to navigate housing affordability crisis
stories.summary: Camber Property Group has hired attorney James Allen as Senior Counsel to manage affordable housing and community development transactions across New York state and the tri-state region. Allen decamped from real estate law firm Hirschen Singer & Epstein and previously served as an associate at Nixon Peabody and senior staff attorney for the New York Court of Appeals. Allen noted that developers are expanding project types and geographic footprint to address the housing affordability crisis.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact. However, the hire signals Camber's strategic focus on scaling affordable housing development and navigating complex tax-credit, regulatory, and subsidy structures across NY/tri-state—suggesting multifamily developers should prioritize in-house or specialized legal expertise for affordable/mixed-income programs as subsidy competition intensifies and deals grow more complex.

stories.title: Selldorf Architects Renews 14K-SF 860 Broadway Lease for 10 Years
stories.excerpt: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects has renewed its 10-year, 13,815-square-foot lease at Gordon Property Group’s 860 Broadway. Selldorf has called the Flatiron District’s 860 Broadway home for the last two decades, according to landlord brokerage Colliers. The asking rent was not disclosed. However, the average asking rent for office space in Midtown South was $79.41 per square foot, with Class A office space asking an average of $97.22 per foot and Class B space asking $79.96 during the second quarter, according to Colliers data. Seth Hecht from Colliers represented Gordon Property in this deal, while the tenant was represented by Erik Schmall and Scott Weiss from Savills. “860 Broadway is one of Manhattan’s iconic office buildings, and its location continues to make it a highly desirable destination for creative and innovative companies,” Hecht said in a statement announcing the renewal. “When a firm as globally respected as Selldorf Architects commits to another decade in the building, it speaks to both the property’s enduring appeal and the long-term strength of this market.” Savills did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. “Our focus has always been on owning and operating buildings for the long term,” Tim Gordon, managing director of Gordon Property Group, said in the statement. “Creating an environment where great companies choose to stay and grow is the ultimate measure of our success, and we’re proud that 860 Broadway continues to earn that kind of commitment.” Selldorf Architects was founded by Annabelle Selldorf in New York City in 1988, according to the company website. The firm has worked on a number of prestigious projects, including the Frick Collection, the Chateau Haut-Brion — a 16th century estate near Bordeaux in France – and the Museum of Contemporary Art in San Diego. stories.summary: Selldorf Architects renewed its 10-year, 13,815-square-foot lease at Gordon Property Group's 860 Broadway in the Flatiron District, following two decades of occupancy. The asking rent was not disclosed; however, Colliers data from Q2 showed average Midtown South office asking rents of $79.41 per square foot, with Class A averaging $97.22 per foot. Colliers represented the landlord; Savills represented the tenant.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. However, long-term renewal by an architecture firm in prime Midtown South location suggests professional-services office demand remains resilient in iconic Manhattan buildings, though does not signal broader office market recovery; implications for residential developers are indirect and related to talent retention and long-term office-to-conversion risk in secondary office stock.
